query: Earlier refractory high-entropy alloys illustrate persistent trade-offs: MoNbTaW and MoNbTaVW retained good yield strength from 600 to 1600 °C, with MoNbTaVW reaching 842 MPa at 1000 °C, but both had poor room-temperature fracture toughness and high density; HfNbTaTiZr showed room-temperature ductility above 50% and a yield strength of 929 MPa but only 295 MPa at 1000 °C; and as-cast HfMoTaTiZr achieved about 1600 MPa at room temperature and 855 MPa at elevated temperature but retained a density of 10.21 g cm−3. Given the constraint that density must be reduced without sacrificing the strong room- and high-temperature mechanical performance of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr, what single intervention should be tested? Provide a mechanistic hypothesis, predicted outcomes relative to the as-cast baseline, explicit temperature and loading boundary conditions, supporting evidence from the preceding RHEA results, and a controlled experiment with quantitative rejection criteria that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Partial replacement of Mo with Nb in as-cast HfMoTaTiZr will lower the overall alloy density while maintaining at least 90% of its original room-temperature and high-temperature yield strengths.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr with reported density of ~10.21 g/cm³, yield strength ~1600 MPa at 25 °C, and ~855 MPa at 1000 °C.
generation.intervention: Substitute up to 20 at.% of Mo with Nb in the as-cast HfMoTaTiZr system.
generation.conditions: Same casting method and post-processing as the baseline; mechanical tests at 25 °C and 1000 °C under a strain rate of 10⁻³ s⁻¹ in inert atmosphere.
generation.structural_mediator: Solid-solution strengthening from the multi-principal element configuration, with partial replacement of heavier Mo by slightly lighter Nb.
generation.mechanism: Nb’s lowered density compared to Mo decreases overall mass while its atomic size and bonding characteristics in a BCC-like matrix continue to promote comparable solid-solution strengthening, preserving mechanical performance.
generation.predicted_outcome: A final density reduced below ~10.0 g/cm³, with yield strength ≥1440 MPa (25 °C) and ≥770 MPa (1000 °C).
generation.baseline: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr having ~10.21 g/cm³ density, 1600 MPa (25 °C) yield strength, 855 MPa (1000 °C) yield strength.
generation.boundary: Test conditions apply to similar compositional homogeneity, casting quality, specimen dimensions, and comparable grain sizes (within ±10% of baseline).
generation.uncertainty: It is unknown whether partial Mo replacement may degrade ductility or long-term creep resistance, as existing data stems from compositions lacking direct Mo–Nb trade-offs.

falsification_experiment.design: Form at least two variants with 10 at.% and 20 at.% Mo replaced by Nb using the same casting protocol as the original alloy, ensuring equivalent microstructural quality. Conduct standard tensile tests at 25 °C and 1000 °C to measure yield strength and elongation.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If final density is not significantly reduced relative to 10.21 g/cm³ or if yield strength drops by more than 10% at 25 °C or by more than 10% at 1000 °C across the tested variants, the hypothesis is falsified.
